human_answer.question: Which short label should both test sessions remember?

observations: Both native interactive UIs started using existing subscription logins.
Codex read-only sandbox and on-request approval. Claude safe-mode and manual permission mode.
Both returned requested readiness text.
Initial sandbox restrictions prevented session writes/network; approved retries outside sandbox succeeded.
Human supplied pigscanfly in Lavish; both interactive sessions returned it.
Both providers exited cleanly and resumed by exact native session ID. Both recalled pigscanfly; Claude verified in its scoped saved transcript.
Relay rejected stale automated input for both providers; Codex was attached by a human during this check.
Phillip reported direct attach, recall and native permission denial in both terminals. Both sentinel files absent.
Codex native rollout records turn_aborted for both denied touch requests despite the UI displaying Ran.
Phillip confirmed revised Ctrl-] works for both clients.
Human reattachment during an automated draft changed the epoch; automated submit was rejected. Partial prompt reconciliation remains a production requirement.
Both old runtime processes exited with status 0; relay still reported assignment unaccepted.
Passive hooks on both exact native versions emitted SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop with structured recall envelope, and PermissionRequest.
Codex emitted Interrupt when the harness canceled a pending native permission request.
Both live structured recall envelopes passed separate owner checks for expected native session, assignment ID and human-selected label.
Claude ran harmless sleep 15 without a prompt; manual permission mode does not imply every command prompts. A Write request produced the permission event.
Both provider hooks produced explicit waiting_for_user envelopes for the actual adapter decision. A stopped turn can therefore mean waiting, not completed.
Claude tool-result transcript records harness cancellation as an error; no Interrupt hook was observed in this configured probe.
A stale-result bug was found and corrected: a new UserPromptSubmit invalidates the previous Stop candidate. Both interrupted/current incomplete probes now remain unaccepted.

Final decision acknowledged by Claude. Codex did not acknowledge: a native rate-limit model-switch dialog intercepted input. Visible selection retained current model and chose never show again. Native dispatch confirmation must not be inferred from PTY write success.
Both hook-probe runtime processes exited with status 0.
Confirmed hide_rate_limit_model_nudge=true after dialog interception; restored false with user-approved scoped repair so rate-limit reminders remain visible.
